verdict.rationale: LangSmith's docs say you can run evaluations on curated datasets to create experiments and to "compare versions, benchmark performance, and catch regressions." They also list a pairwise comparison evaluator and the ability to compare traces in the UI or API. However, the evidence never describes a side-by-side view of experiment results, so the 'side by side' part is only implied. Missing for 10: documentation of a side-by-side experiment comparison view (diffing scores and outputs per example across runs), and independent or hands-on corroboration of regression detection between prompt or model versions.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can compare eval runs side by side to catch regressions between prompt or model versions

citations.quote: Run evaluations on curated datasets during development to compare versions, benchmark performance, and catch regressions.
Execute your application on the dataset to create an experiment.
Create evaluators to score performance: Human review, Code rules, LLM-as-judge, Pairwise comparison
Filter, export, share, and compare traces via the UI or API.
